_doc: The case bank. TRIAGED 2026-07-28 against the rebuilt qualifying filter in knowledge/CASE_CRAFT.md. The filter added a HARD GATE that a case must have a disclosed cost class AND a disclosed decision-to-working timeline, because if we cannot tell the reader what it took, it is a story and not a plan. NONE of the 16 seeded cases carried a cost, and their 'timeline' fields held an announcement date rather than a duration, so all 16 were demoted from candidate to lead. They are not deleted: each carries a `qualification` block naming exactly which filter parts hold and exactly what a scout must go find, which is a far better starting point than an empty bank. Ship-ready count is 0, so the first run under the new contract triggers a full Phase 1 restock, which is the correct and honest state. Entries also predate the 2024-or-later recency rule and the 50-1000 employee band; both are recorded per entry.

cases.size: 700 plus trucks, 650 plus drivers, family founded 1955
cases.bottleneck: Rising insurance costs, paper heavy back office, overdue preventive maintenance, no visibility into driver risk or trailer utilization.
cases.build: Samsara AI dash cams with automated driver coaching, telematics, driver app, smart trailer dormancy reports, plus an internal Fraley Score driver performance system built on top.

numbers.what: insurance cost reduction 2020 to 2023 while the market rose about 20 percent
back office admin savings, 99 percent less paperwork processing time
fewer overdue preventive maintenance checks
total estimated annual savings across programs

cases.skepticism: Vendor case study. The insurance number is the most concrete and externally anchored line. The rest are company estimates. Label vendor sourced.
cases.alaska_translation: Alaska trucking and air cargo run the same math with harsher roads and higher stakes. Insurance, maintenance compliance, and back office paperwork are universal fleet bottlenecks.
cases.notes: Strongest single company story in the bank for relatability. Alternates surfaced but not fetched, Halvor Lines (Netradyne), Dohrn Transfer (Samsara).

cases.size: 160 refrigerated trucks, three DCs, 2,400 customers, 8,000 plus deliveries a week, founded 1943
cases.bottleneck: Static hand built routes. Customers got appended to routes so drivers crossed town and back. Two to three route planners per distribution center.
cases.build: OptimoRoute algorithmic route optimization with delivery time windows, unload times, and what if simulation for prospective customers.

numbers.what: fleet wide mileage reduction on 4.6 million annual miles
lower driver costs
more delivery capacity, about 330 extra deliveries a day, same fleet
on time rate improvement

cases.skepticism: Vendor case study with a named logistics manager and unusually specific operational detail. No independent audit.
cases.alaska_translation: Anchorage food and freight distribution runs the same static route trap. Percent level mileage cuts are real money at Alaska fuel and labor rates. Same math as the snowplow route studies.
cases.notes: Family produce house archetype. Pairs with the public sector plow route evidence for a boring optimization pays theme.

cases.size: About 1.5 million background checks a month for 100,000 plus businesses
cases.bottleneck: 2 percent of background check records are messy free text needing classification into 230 categories. GPT-4 hit 88 percent overall, 82 on hard cases, 7 to 15 second latency, 7,000 to 12,000 dollars a month.
cases.build: Fine tuned Llama-3 8B on their own data via Predibase, served on a single A100 GPU.

numbers.what: overall accuracy after fine tuning, 85 on the hardest cases
latency, roughly 30x faster
serving cost, roughly 5x cheaper than GPT-4

cases.skepticism: Original reporting by Computerworld with before and after baselines, though the underlying numbers are self reported by Checkr's ML engineer.
cases.alaska_translation: The cleanest public proof that a small model fine tuned on your own data can beat the big general model on cost, speed, and accuracy for one narrow job. The ownership story, your model, your data, costs that fall.
cases.notes: The model tuning capability file anchor. Over the size band as a tech firm, use for the mechanism with the size caveat said plainly.

cases.size: Small contract CNC shop, est 2007, Swiss lathes
cases.bottleneck: Undetected tool breakage on automated machines. Roughly a third of parts per shift lost to scrap, an hour per shift sorting good from bad, machines over provisioned at 200 percent capacity to absorb waste.
cases.build: MachineMetrics tool monitoring, sensorless high frequency data from the machine control, ML detects imminent tool failure and feed holds the machine before it wrecks parts.

numbers.what: saved per machine per year
accuracy predicting tool failure

cases.alaska_translation: Any Alaska shop running machines that break expensive things quietly, machining, wood, food processing lines. The pattern is listen to the machine, stop it before the damage.
cases.notes: Small shop archetype, enabled lights out running.

numbers.what: complete chart time

cases.alaska_translation: Ambient scribes are now buyable off the shelf, which makes this THE entry story for independent Anchorage practices. Documentation is where healthcare ROI concentrates.
cases.notes: Non tech operator building rather than buying, early and credible.

cases.company: The Wilson Companies (Wilson Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Electric Inc.)
cases.size: 200 plus employees, 40 plus million dollars revenue, founded 1958 by Ralph and Theresa Wilson, third generation family ownership
cases.bottleneck: The phones. Nights, weekends and overflow calls went to an outside answering service, the raw inbound booking rate was 27 percent, and the call centre ran 18 CSRs.
cases.build: Bought Avoca AI, an off the shelf home services voice platform, and configured it. No engineers hired, no model trained in house. The voice agent answers, handles routine booking end to end and writes the appointment into the CRM. It hands off to a live human CSR when it detects a frustrated caller. A second component scores every call for coaching. Started on nights, weekends and overflow only, then widened.
cases.ladder_rung: 4 (workflow). Humans designed the steps. Anything outside the drawn path stops at a checkpoint and goes to a person. Vendor markets it as an AI workforce, an AI CSR and agents, which is rung 5 language for a rung 4 build.
cases.timeline: About two weeks to onboard, about 90 days to work well
cases.cost: About 3,500 dollars a month, replacing an 8,000 dollars a month outside answering service, as recollected by the buyer on the record
cases.skepticism: Primary source is a podcast the operator himself hosts and one episode carries a sponsor credit to the vendor. The cost is the buyer's recollection and he says on the record he does not actually know the figure. The 18 to 10 CSR reduction and the roughly 30k a month are not attributed to the AI alone by anyone on the record. Machine transcripts are garbled. Every number must ride with an operator-self-reported label.
cases.alaska_translation: Anchorage mechanical, plumbing and HVAC contractors run the identical after hours phone problem, and heating season makes the no heat call at 9pm an emergency with a price attached.
cases.note: SELECTED for case file 2. The vendor's own admission that full autonomy books roughly 5 percent lower than the hybrid design is the best rung 4 versus rung 5 teaching artifact any run has found.

cases.size: Just over 180 team members (FreightWaves 2021), 164 drivers and 158 power units on an FMCSA MCS-150 filed 05/08/2026, about 170 trucks per trade press. Size filter PROVEN.
cases.bottleneck: Dispatchers paired drivers to loads by hand and by feel. VP of Operations Deen Albert on the record, 'We were dispatching in a reactionary type of format.'
cases.build: Bought Optimal Dynamics and fed it live data from their existing McLeod Loadmaster TMS. It weighs driver home time, headhaul and backhaul timing, profitability and asset utilization, then recommends which driver takes which load. A dispatcher accepts or vetoes. Created a new internal role, Optimal Solutions Specialist.
cases.ladder_rung: 4 (workflow) with a real human veto. Note the contrast worth teaching later: Optimal Dynamics' March 2026 Decision-Native Agentic System launch is a genuine rung 5 product, while what Grand Island ran in 2024 is a clean rung 4.
cases.timeline: About a year of internal readiness work, partnership January 2024, live April 2024
cases.cost: NONE. NO COST ANYWHERE IN PUBLIC.
cases.named_human: Deen Albert, VP of Operations (note: Overdrive spells it Dean, two other outlets plus his own profile say Deen)
cases.skepticism: DEAD ON COST after an exhaustive dedicated chase 2026-08-15. The CCJ Innovators profile, retrieved past its 403 wall via r.jina.ai, contains the words cost, price, pricing, paid, pay, invest, investment, ROI, dollar, subscription and contract exactly zero times. Optimal Dynamics has no pricing page (404), its Capterra listing is dead, its case study is gated behind a lead form. A Forbes piece on sibling customer D.M. Bowman says with load planning it is difficult to quantify the exact return on investment. Only remaining routes are the gated PDF and a 30 minute fireside video whose transcript could not be extracted.
cases.alaska_translation: Alaska freight, fuel distribution and air cargo run the same dispatch board problem with harsher roads and thinner margins for error.
cases.note: Everything is in excellent shape except the one hard gate. Numbers include 84 percent of loads matching platform recommendations from week two (FleetOwner Jan 2025) rising to about 93 percent of dispatch decisions by mid April (CCJ Innovators) - different metrics, never present as one. Excellent named limit: they discovered the organisation was not ready and the VP flew to another carrier to watch it work before committing. Revisit the day a cost-disclosed carrier surfaces.

cases.size: NOT VERIFIED, the single biggest gap. Municipally owned since 1891, 9.5 square mile territory, 217 miles of overhead circuit, 7,000 poles, about 16,000 assets.
cases.bottleneck: Nobody can see the top of a pole from the ground. Per the utility director, structural problems have sat there for 30 to 40 years before causing a disruption.
cases.build: Bought eSmart Systems Grid Vision on a five year SaaS contract. CBPU flies its own drones. The model scores images for defects. Trained analysts review EVERY flagged finding before it becomes a work order. Validated findings flow into the existing work order system. Vendor used train the trainer rather than staffing it for them.
cases.ladder_rung: 3 wrapped in 4. A vision model called at one fixed point, inside fixed steps with a human checkpoint before any work order. Notably nobody in any source calls it an agent.
cases.timeline: Began exploring 2023, pilot 2024, in house drone flights over about 400 poles summer 2025, five year contract board approved and reported 1 January 2026
cases.cost: 248,000 dollars for a five year contract, roughly 50,000 a year. PUBLIC RECORD, board approved.
cases.named_human: Paul Jakubczak, Utility Director, 'If this helps to eliminate even one outage, it's well worth that'
cases.skepticism: TWO GATES OPEN. Filter 4 fails, there is no measured before and after. 4,600 images narrowed to 400 actionable items is a throughput number. Nothing states inspection hours, cost per pole or outages avoided before versus after. Filter 1 unverified, no fetched page gives an employee count. Also a municipal board is a step away from Dana, who owns a private business. Third source is a vendor byline by an eSmart VP.
cases.alaska_translation: Railbelt co-ops, pipeline and facility inspection contractors carry the identical cannot see the top of the asset problem, with worse access and weather.
cases.note: To make shippable a fact-checker needs CBPU board minutes for FTE count and confirmation of the 248,000, plus one before/after number. Found via the two-step that is now the highest-yield craft this repo owns.

cases.size: About 200 employees, three facilities totalling 361,500 square feet, founded 1997 by Clinton Beeland, 200 plus customers
cases.bottleneck: Employees exhausted numerous hours every week processing printed batch sheets that included non-standard client data.
cases.build: GaMEP scoped three projects. dataPARC real time data software across two facilities plus a replaced quality management system. Separately a generative AI pilot with vendor Vieaura to convert printed batch sheets into standardised digital workflows.
cases.ladder_rung: 1 to 2 for the part carrying the numbers. The Vieaura piece would be rung 3.
cases.timeline: Data software March 2022, QMS after a June 2022 assessment, AI batch sheet project indexed as starting February 2024
cases.cost: 300,000 dollars across two facilities, BUT it bought the plumbing, not the AI
cases.named_human: Mitchell Tatar, Process Engineer (quote is a thank you note about GaMEP, describes neither the bottleneck nor a result)
cases.skepticism: KILLED BY FOUR INDEPENDENT SCOUTS on 2026-08-15 for the same reason. The 300,000 bought dataPARC plus a QMS, which is rung 1 to 2, and all three headline numbers (51 percent reduction in price of non-conformance, 20 percent production capacity increase, 30,000 a month from a prevented chiller failure) attach to that plumbing. The generative AI work is STILL FUTURE TENSE as of the NIST page's own updated date of 29 April 2026, verbatim 'Tatar expects to convert their printed batch sheets into automated digital workflows in the next few months'. Vieaura confirms customer names are under NDA and CJB appears nowhere on its site. gamep.org rendered blank on three separate attempts across two waves.
cases.alaska_translation: n/a until the AI actually ships
cases.note: Company shape is ideal. Revisit in one to two quarters or get it by interview. Do not ship future tense as a result.

cases.size: NOT STATED. Described as a certified small business, may sit under the 50 employee floor.
cases.bottleneck: Staff retrieving technical data from internal purchase orders, MIL-SPECs and inspection reports slowed RFQ response.
cases.build: A secure ON-PREMISES AI chatbot over internal documents, plus Microsoft Power Automate RPA for AR updates and delivery reminders and two Power BI dashboards, via TMAC.
cases.named_human: Derek Boone, Owner (quote is a thank you to TMAC about tooling)
cases.skepticism: Fails the hard gate outright, no cost and no timeline. The page's own words are prototype and proof of concept, which is a demo not production. Only numbers are 12,000 dollars in ESTIMATED annual savings and improved process time by 10 percent, no base, no denominator.
cases.alaska_translation: ANC subsidiaries and engineering firms carry the same buried-spec retrieval problem.
cases.note: On premises retrieval over MIL-SPECs would be a strong P2 case if an interview produced cost, timeline, headcount and production volume. One of only three AI stories in NIST's entire 1,067 story MEP archive.

cases.company: Viking Group Inc. (Todd Rogers), 17 unit Donatos Pizza franchisee
cases.size: 17 restaurant units
cases.bottleneck: Phone order taking load in the restaurants.
cases.build: Revmo AI for phone order taking.
cases.named_human: Todd Rogers, quoted in a Multi Unit Franchisee roundtable saying the system improves order accuracy and creates a quieter restaurant environment
cases.skepticism: No cost, no timeline, no measured before and after at his 17 units. The chain level Donatos and Revmo numbers that exist come from a joint PR release and belong to a company well over 1,000 employees, so they cannot be borrowed for the franchisee.
cases.alaska_translation: Anchorage multi location food service and quick service operators carry the same phone load.
cases.note: Right size band and a named operator. Worth an interview. The Multi Unit Franchisee roundtable format is good for FINDING named operators at our size but never asks what anything cost. Try recorded franchisee convention panels instead.

interview_leads.why: Fisheries EM provider using computer vision in Gulf of Alaska pollock EM since the 1990s era of observer work. The most Alaska native AI operations story available, no public numbers, worth a direct interview.

paywalled_leads: CCJ Samsara dashcam crash rate study
par_note: 2026-08-15: bank restocked by two waves (7 scouts). Ship-ready count is 1, still far below par of 8. The structural finding of the run is that every hunting ground carries exactly one half of what the filter needs and never the same half: trade press names the operator and omits the price, public record names the price and omits the deployment, vendor libraries describe the build and omit both. The one ground that delivered BOTH was an operator-to-operator PODCAST (ownedandoperated.com), where peers disclose casually because the audience would smell a dodge. That is the highest-yield ground this repo has found and wave three should mine it and its equivalents in freight, distribution and clinic operations.
